signal: Compyl raised a $12M Series A to accelerate go-to-market and is expanding into healthcare, fintech and APAC in 2026

email.body1:
Stephen, saw Compyl raised its $12M Series A to accelerate GTM and is pushing into healthcare, fintech, and APAC.

Expanding into new regulated segments that fast usually means more strategic accounts in play than reps can cover before the new motion ramps, and that is where deals stall. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up on its own, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for Compyl off your hiring and tech-stack signals, accounts showing them progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Stephen, quick follow-up for Compyl.

With GTM expansion underway, pipeline targets tend to climb faster than headcount in your strategic territory. Most teams cannot say exactly how many meetings they need to hit the new number, so the gap shows up late and the quarter turns into a scramble.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I will walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings Compyl needs to close that gap this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Stephen, last bit of proof for Compyl.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and could not hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Compyl's reply rate likely compares to other Series-A startups. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through it?
email.body4:
Stephen, I will stop reaching out on this one, but did not want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling strategic-account pipeline without adding headcount is not a priority this quarter, no problem at all. Timing is everything during an expansion push, and that stretch is its own kind of busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to your strategic motion? I will tailor it to Compyl either way.
